title: An out-of-state practitioner's Schedule II prescription may be filled only if issued within the preceding five days
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(a) a prescription for a controlled substance may be issued only by a practitioner who is authorized to prescribe controlled substances and registered pursuant to chapter 94C. Section 18(d) provides that a prescription for a nonnarcotic substance in Schedule II may also be issued by a practitioner who is licensed and authorized to engage in prescriptive practice and registered in another state where the practitioner resides or practices, if required, and registered under federal law to write prescriptions. Section 18(d1/2), except as provided in s. 18A, provides the same for a narcotic substance in Schedule II where the practitioner is so licensed and registered in Maine or in a state contiguous with the commonwealth. Each subsection is only for the purpose of authorizing the filling, within the commonwealth, of prescriptions issued within the preceding five days, and does not authorize the practitioner to possess, administer or dispense controlled substances under s. 9 or to practice within the commonwealth. A Schedule II prescription from an out-of-state practitioner who is not registered under chapter 94C is therefore fillable in Massachusetts only under s. 18(d) or s. 18(d1/2), and only if it was issued within the preceding five days, whether the fill is full or partial.
exam_relevance: Tests that the five-day figure on the out-of-state Schedule II routes limits filling the prescription at all, not only the initial partial dispensing, so a full fill is equally unavailable after the fifth day unless the prescriber is registered under chapter 94C.

numeric_facts.fact: Window within which an out-of-state practitioner's Schedule II prescription may be filled in Massachusetts
numeric_facts.conditions: The prescription must have been issued within the preceding five days; applies on the s. 18(d) nonnarcotic and s. 18(d1/2) narcotic routes

exceptions: A practitioner who is authorized to prescribe controlled substances and registered under chapter 94C issues under s. 18(a), and the five-day filling window of s. 18(d) and s. 18(d1/2) does not govern that prescription.
The narcotic route in s. 18(d1/2) reaches only practitioners registered in Maine or a state contiguous with the commonwealth, and is subject to s. 18A.
common_confusions: Reading the five-day figure as limiting only an initial partial fill, when s. 18(d) and s. 18(d1/2) authorize filling at all only of prescriptions issued within the preceding five days.
Treating the 30-day Schedule II validity period as available to an out-of-state prescription that depends on s. 18(d) or s. 18(d1/2).
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(a), (d) and (d1/2) read in the current text on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
